summary: The note explains how automation, robotics and AI are changing manufacturing employment, shifting demand from routine manual roles to technicians, analysts and engineers. It argues that upskilling is the key to adaptation and covers corporate training, scholarships, online courses, on-the-job mentoring and government grants. It also stresses collaboration among manufacturers, educators, government and technology providers.
one_line: Guide to how automation is reshaping manufacturing jobs and how workers can adapt through upskilling, training programs, and government and industry support.
key_facts: As of October 3, 2023, the International Federation of Robotics reported a surge in industrial robot installations, concentrated in automotive, electronics, and heavy machinery sectors.
AI systems can predict maintenance needs, streamline supply chains, and inform decisions about production processes.

Dr. Emily Sanderson, an economist and automation expert, says some roles are diminishing but new categories of jobs are emerging that focus on overseeing, programming, and maintaining automated systems.
Between January and August of 2023, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported a downturn in routine manual positions and a swell in demand for technicians, analysts, and engineers.

Industrial psychologist Olivia Brown, in conversation on September 15, 2023, said in-demand skills balance technical knowledge like programming or data analysis with soft skills such as problem-solving and collaboration.
SteelCo has invested over $20 million since September 2023 into its 'Future Skills Academy', which trains workers in robotics, AI, and advanced materials.
The 'NextGen Machinists Scholarship' was introduced on September 22, 2023 to support manufacturing upskilling.
AutoFab CEO Maria Alvarez said in a statement on October 6, 2023 that the company pairs each employee with a mentor and provides hands-on training with the latest technology.
Coursera, edX, and Udemy offer courses from basic computer skills to advanced programming for manufacturing technologies.
Since September 2023 there has been a notable rise in specialized online platforms catering exclusively to the manufacturing sector, offering tutorials, webinars, and certifications.
On October 1, 2023, the government launched the 'Manufacturing Modernization Grant' for small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to adopt automation and subsidize employee training.
Jessica Lin, a workforce development coordinator, organized a sector-wide summit on September 28, 2023 focused on sharing best practices and co-creating solutions.
